title: Telemetry snooze policy + ML anomaly harness for burn-rate alerting
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: We have recurring false-positive burn-rate pages during scheduled workload shifts (batch flushes, nightly reindex, customer migrations). This causes oncall fatigue and masks real degradations. Goal: implement a telemetry-aware snooze/quiet window mechanism combined with an ML-based anomaly harness that can downgrade noisy but expected burn-rate blips and surface correlated, actionable incidents. Deliverables: 1) a snooze policy engine that can be applied per-service/route with calendar and signal-driven triggers; 2) a signal fusion pipeline that correlates traces, error logs, and token-level metrics to produce context for the alerting decision; 3) an ML anomaly harness that scores burn-rate events for signal novelty and operational risk and annotates alerts; 4) dashboard and runbook changes to expose why an alert was suppressed or elevated.
acceptance_criteria: Snooze policy can be configured per service/route via Console with calendar rules and signal predicates
Burn-rate alert pipeline consults the snooze engine before paging and will suppress/attenuate alerts with clear audit logs
Anomaly harness returns a numeric novelty/risk score and a top-3 correlated signals list within 3s for each burn-rate candidate
Dashboards show suppressed alerts with root-cause hints and links to top traces/related logs
End-to-end automated test demonstrates a scheduled maintenance window where synthetic high burn-rate is suppressed and a real latency spike still pages

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-suppression could hide real incidents. Mitigation: conservative default policies, incremental rollout with canary percentage and automatic fallback to paging after a maximum hold period.

Risk: ML harness false negatives early in deployment. Mitigation: ML labeled-mode initially (score-only) and human-in-the-loop feedback to collect training data; require score thresholds + corroborating signals to suppress paging.
Risk: Increased alert latency due to enrichment calls. Mitigation: cache recent enrichment results, run async enrichment with best-effort early-exit if deadline exceeded.
Risk: Multi-tenant policy complexity. Mitigation: scope policies to tenant or tenant-group and provide clear inheritance/override rules in Console.
metrics: Reduction in pages per week for scheduled maintenance windows (target: 80% reduction)
False suppression rate (target: <1% of suppressed that should have paged)
Median added alert decision latency (target: <50ms for snooze check + <300ms for enrichment/ML)
Time to correlated trace link generation (target: <3s)
Oncall time saved metric piloted for two teams
implementation_notes: Snooze policy schema will be stored in Config Service with versioning. Policy evaluation occurs in the alerting pipeline before burn-rate compute decides to page.
Signal fusion implemented as streaming enrichment: use existing trace-ingest Kafka topic and a lookaside aggregation in Redis for last-10m error/token deltas per route.
ML harness to start with a lightweight isolation-forest change detector over fused features; retrain cadence weekly and keep a score cache.
All suppressed alerts must emit an audit span and write a suppression-event to telemetry (for dashboards and postmortems).

decisions: Start ML in score-only mode (no automatic suppression) for 2 production cycles to collect labels.
Use isolation-forest for novelty detection initially for low compute overhead; move to a supervised model after collecting labeled events.
Audit events for all suppressions are required and retained for 90 days for postmortem and model training.
